title: staged-multi-arm-traffic-reconciler-with-timestamped-cohort-leases
author: Maya Singh
body: Summary: Introduces a staged multi-arm traffic reconciler that coordinates timed cohort leases and deterministic reconciliation to support multi-variant canaries, A/B experiments, and shadow-to-canary promotions with safe automatic rollback windows. Motivation: Current rollout controller optimizes single-path canaries but struggles when multiple concurrent arms (A/B/n) need coordinated swaps, timed lease expiry, and deterministic conflict resolution across regions and Dedicated clusters. This PR implements a lease-based temporal reconciler that: 1) assigns timestamped leases to cohort partitions, 2) uses a conflict-free reconciliation loop to avoid oscillation when multiple controllers observe different states, 3) provides a promotion API for shadow arms to be fast-swapped into serving lanes when metric gates pass, and 4) exposes fine-grained probe hooks for safety gates and automatic rollback triggers. Design highlights: - Lease model: cohorts receive monotonic timestamped leases (lease_id + expiry_ts). A reconciler accepts an action only when local time < expiry_ts and lease origin matches expected coordinator. - Deterministic reconciliation: deterministic tie-breaker (lease_id + origin priority) prevents flip-flop across regions when controller heartbeats cross. - Multi-arm state machine: supports an arbitrary number of arms, tracks per-arm telemetry windows, and allows staged promotion where arm B can be promoted to 30% then 60% with automatic safety holdpoints. - Shadow promotion: a shadow arm can be promoted into live traffic via promoteShadow API; traffic migrates through an atomic staged plan that respects session affinity and KV-cache compatibility checks. - Rollback orchestration: rollback plans are checkpointed; a heuristic auto-rollback triggers on SLO/mortality gates with a configurable grace window and therapeutical cool-down to avoid thrashing. Backwards compatibility: - Controller exposes a feature flag rollout.v2.multiaarm=false for gradual enablement. - Existing single-arm canaries remain on the legacy controller unless the flag is enabled for a rollout. Files changed (high-level): - pkg/rollout/reconciler.go: new reconciler core and lease reconciliation primitives. - pkg/rollout/lease_store.go: in-memory + persistent lease store adapters (etcd-backed adapter stubbed for testing). - api/v1/rollout.proto: adds MultiArmPlan, LeaseRef, PromoteShadow RPC. - internal/telemetry/metrics.go: adds arms_active, arm_promotion_latency, lease_conflicts_total. - console/src/components/RolloutTimeline.tsx: UI for multi-arm timelines and lease status overlays. - e2e/tests/multiarm_rollout.spec.ts: end-to-end scenarios including failover and auto-rollback. - docker/dev/rollout-integration.Dockerfile: lightweight image used by CI integration. Tests and validation: - Unit tests: comprehensive unit coverage for reconciler state transitions and tie-breaker determinism. - Integration tests: e2e scenarios emulate cross-region controller heartbeats with adjustable clock skew to validate deterministic outcomes. - Load tests: lightweight perf bench shows <3% overhead on control plane CPU at 10k rollouts/min. Migration and rollout plan: - Feature-gated behind rollout.v2.multiaarm. - Canary rollout to internal teams for 2 weeks; monitor arm_promotion_latency and lease_conflicts_total. - If lease_conflicts_total spikes >5% for 10m, automatic rollback to legacy controller (operational playbook included). Operational docs and runbook: - Added runbook section in docs/rollouts/multiarm-runbook.md explaining investigation steps, key metrics, and emergency disable flags. - Console changes include a lease inspector panel and hazard indicators when a plan exceeds staged time windows. Checklist: - [x] Core reconciler implementation - [x] Proto and API changes with backwards-compat stubs - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Console visualization and operator controls - [x] Runbook and migration notes - [x] Benchmarks and CI passing Known limitations: - Etcd-backed lease store adapter is stubbed; production adapter will be wired in a follow-up (ENG-10014) to avoid coupling with this PR. - KV-cache compatibility checks rely on a per-model capability vector that will be expanded in the model-registry follow-up. Related work: ENG-9821 (multi-arm rollout design doc), ENG-10014 (persistent lease-store integration). Release notes: Implements multi-arm staged traffic reconciler with timestamped cohort leases, shadow promotion API, and automatic rollback orchestration. Backwards-incompatible changes: none (feature gated).
commits: Wire up proto changes and PromoteShadow RPC
Add in-memory lease store and unit tests
Console timeline visualization and lease inspector
Integration tests for cross-region heartbeats and deterministic reconciliation
Address reviewer feedback: add metrics, tighten tie-breaker, add feature flag
review_comments: Aisha Brown: Please clarify how the tie-breaker behaves if clocks diverge significantly. Suggest adding a monotonic counter fallback.
Maya Singh: Replied - added monotonic lease_id increment and fallback path; updated reconciler.go lines 142-170 to use monotonic_id when clock skew > 5s.
Diego Marquez: Can we add a metrics tag for origin region to help debug cross-region conflicts?
Maya Singh: Added origin_region label to lease_conflicts_total and promoted metric changes to telemetry/metrics.go
Lin Zhu: Integration tests are flakey on CI due to Docker networking timeouts; suggest increasing default timeouts and adding retry semantics.
Maya Singh: Increased e2e retry backoff and added a dedicated CI job with more generous timeouts. Reran tests; green.
Omar Patel: Small nit - prefer feature flag name rollout.v2.multiarm to be consistent with other flags.
Maya Singh: Renamed flag to rollout.v2.multiarm and updated docs and console wiring.
ci_summary: Integration (e2e): pass (2 retries added to flaky scenario)
release_notes:
- Add staged multi-arm traffic reconciler with timestamped cohort leases
- Add PromoteShadow API to promote shadow arms into live traffic
- Console visualization for multi-arm timelines and lease inspector
- Runbook for operator procedures and automatic rollback triggers
